# Report: `region.fasta` (3,000 bp, `>region_006`)

## Summary
Nothing exotic — no transposon, no CRISPR array, no tandem or inverted repeats, no CpG island, no signal peptide. What *does* stand out: **the fragment is essentially a protein‑coding gene cluster, and it all runs off the reverse (minus) strand.** Three ORFs tile ~87% of the 3 kb.

## Composition (boring, as expected)
- 3,000 bp, **GC 54.9%**; GC skew −0.07, AT skew −0.04 (no strand compositional bias).
- **CpG O/E = 1.28** (287 CpGs vs 225 expected) → *no* CpG suppression, so not vertebrate/methylated DNA.
- Longest homopolymer = 6 bp. **No exact repeat ≥ 12 bp anywhere** (forward or inverted), and only 4 duplicated 11‑mers vs ~1 expected → no repeat‑type element of any kind.

## The notable feature: three ORFs, all on the minus strand

| Feature | Forward coords (1‑based) | Len | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Gene A** CDS | **1484–2935** (minus) | 483 aa | ATG at 2933‑2935, TAG stop at 1484‑1486 |
| Gene A upstream | 2936–3000 | 65 nt | cut off by the fragment edge |
| *intergenic* | **1372–1483** | 112 nt | AT‑rich trough, **38.4% GC** (lowest in the fragment; poly‑T run at 1463‑1468) |
| Gene B 5'UTR | 1177–1371 | 195 nt | |
| **Gene B** CDS | **295–1176** (minus) | 293 aa | ATG at 1174‑1176, TGA stop at 295‑297 |
| *intergenic* | **286–294** | 9 nt | |
| **Gene C** CDS (partial) | **1–285** (minus) | ≥95 aa | ATG at 283‑285, no stop before the fragment ends |

Head‑to‑tail on one strand with 9–112 nt spacers = a classic bacterial operon/cluster. The plus strand carries nothing of consequence (its longest ORF is 108 aa, fwd 1478‑1804, which is nested inside Gene A and is within the chance range).

## Why I believe the two big ORFs are real
Against 3,000 order‑5 Markov shuffles of this same sequence (preserving base and 5‑mer composition):

| Statistic | Query | Shuffle control |
|---|---|---|
| Longest stop‑free ORF, 6 frames | **504 aa** (483 aa with ATG) | median 178, p95 260, **max 466** → p < 1/3000 |
| Codons sitting in ≥100‑aa stop‑free runs | **986** | median 239, p95 475 → p < 1/3000 |
| # complete ATG‑initiated ORFs ≥100 aa | 4 | median 2, p95 5 → *not* significant |

So it's the **lengths**, not the count, that are decisive. Both CDSs also show a clear 3‑periodic codon‑position bias (Gene A GC1/2/3 = 67.4/40.7/61.6; Gene B = 61.2/39.1/60.2), the signature of protein coding sequence.

## Protein‑level observations (tentative — no database here to name domains)
- **Gene A** (483 aa): very helix‑rich (L 66, A 45, G 47, only 5 Cys, 6 Tyr). Max 19‑aa Kyte–Doolittle = 1.69 → **soluble, no TM helix, no signal peptide** (N‑terminus starts MRSLGCSNID…, no positively‑charged hydrophobic core).
- **Gene B** (293 aa): acidic/globular, starts MKQGLEDVSGLLELAVEADDEETFNEA…, max KD 0.62 → soluble.
- Gene A vs Gene B best ungapped identity = **11.9%** → not paralogs.
- Strongly biased codon usage (e.g. CTG 39/66 Leu, GCG 20/45 Ala, TTA only 6/66), which is atypical of AT‑rich generic codon tables.
- Minor caveat: a **GTG** at forward 2992‑2994 would extend Gene A to 502 aa; I used the ATG.

## Caveats
- No organism context or annotation DB available, so I can't assign functions or name the genes — the domain calls above are inference only.
- Gene A's promoter/RBS is beyond the fragment edge (only 65 nt upstream), and Gene C is truncated; extending the fragment would be the single most useful next step.
- Coordinates are 1‑based on the forward strand as read from the FASTA; ORFs are given in reverse orientation (read them as forward 1484→2935 with the complement).
